title: Quantifying Cytoskeleton Dynamics Using Differential Dynamic Microscopy
protocol: Choose the optimal available imaging modality and optical settings.
Determine the range of wavenumbers, q, based on pixel size and total image size.
Confirm that the choice of magnification and field of view are optimal for the experiment.
Use a 60x 1.4 NA objective with an image size of 256 x 256 pixels and a pixel size of 0.83 µm for active actin-microtubule composite network imaging.
Use a 100x 1.4 NA objective with an image size of 512 x 512 pixels and a pixel size of 0.13 µm for bead imaging in vimentin networks.
Calculate the minimum q using the formula 2π/NΔx, where N is the image size (assumed to be square) and Δx is the pixel size.
Determine the maximum q as the minimum value between π/Δx and 2π NA/λ, where NA is the imaging objective's numerical aperture and λ is the wavelength of light.
Consider the range of timescales for investigation.
Ensure DDM analysis is done on sequences of at least 1000 frames.
Determine the appropriate frame rate based on the expected time it will take for sample features to move a distance corresponding to the minimum resolvable length scale.
Acquire image sequences longer than the maximum timescale probed.
Acquire image sequences ideally over 1000 frames based on time and length scales to probe.
Save image sequences as a three-dimensional greyscale TIFF stack.
Alternatively, use ImageJ or another imaging processing program to convert images to a TIFF stack.
If using ND2 files, ensure the nd2reader package is installed.
Make a copy of the example_parameter_file.yml from the PyDDM code repository.
Open the copied YAML file with a text editor like NotePad++ or JupyterLab.
Provide the data directory and file name corresponding to the image sequence in the YAML file.
Under the metadata section, provide the pixel size and frame rate.
Under the Analysis_parameters section, specify details for how the DDM matrix should be calculated.
Provide values for number_lag_times and last_lag_time parameters.
Set number_lag_times to 60.
Set last_lag_time to 1000 frames.
Compute DDM matrix with logarithmic spacing from minimum lag time to last_lag_time.
Fit the DDM matrix or ISF using fitting parameters section details.
Specify the name of the model under the model parameter.
Provide initial guess for each fitting parameter.
Define lower bound for each fitting parameter.
Define upper bound for each fitting parameter.
Initialize an instance of the DDM_Analysis class using a YAML file or a Python dictionary.
Calculate the DDM matrix by running the function calculate_DDM_matrix.
Inspect the returned data structure from the xarray package known as a Dataset.
Note that the dataset includes not only the DDM matrix but also associated variables and metadata.
The data structure is saved to disk in Network Common Data Form (netCDF) format.
Inspect the plots and figures generated, which are also saved as PDF files in the data directory.
If imgsrc://cloudfront.jove.com/files/ftp_upload/63931/63931eq031.png is not reaching a plateau at large q, then use another method for estimating B.
Set the parameter background_method in either the YAML file.
Use the background_method as an optional keyword argument to the function calculate_DDM_matrix.
Initialize an instance of the DDM_Fit class by passing the filename of the YAML file containing image metadata and fitting parameters.
List available models for fitting data by executing print_fitting_models function.
Specify the model to use in the YAML parameter file or through reload_fit_model_by_name function.
Set initial guesses for each parameter using set_parameter_initial_guess function.
Define bounds for each parameter with set_parameter_bounds function.
Execute the fit using the fit function, assigning output to a variable for easy result access.
Generate plots to inspect fits and q-dependence of fit parameters with fit_report function.
Use the xarray function to_netcdf or Python's built-in pickle module to save the xarray dataset to disk.
Use the xarray function open_dataset to load these netCDF files.
Use the function save_fit_results_to_excel to save the fit results, along with the data, to a worksheet file.
